purpose: find and rank ways an attacker can abuse the system before it is built or changed, and tie each to a control and a test
entry_criteria: Architecture or data-flow diagram exists for the feature or system in scope
Assets and data classifications are listed
Accountable security-architect and a developer who knows the design are available
procedure: Draw or confirm the data-flow diagram; mark every trust boundary, entry point, data store and external dependency.
Enumerate threats per element with a named taxonomy (for example STRIDE) and an attacker capability (unauthenticated, authenticated user, insider, compromised dependency).
Score each threat by likelihood and impact on one fixed scale; record the scale in the document.
For each threat above the agreed threshold, name a mitigation, the control that implements it, and the test or scan that will verify it.
Record accepted residual risks with owner, rationale and an expiry date.
Link each mitigation to a backlog item and each verification to a later stage (SAST 99, DAST 100, Penetration Testing 104).
acceptance_criteria: Every trust boundary crossing has at least one enumerated threat or a written reason for none
Every high or critical threat has a mitigation with a verifying test
Every accepted risk has a named owner and an expiry date
Diagram and document are versioned with the design they describe
validation_method: Independent security design review by someone who did not author the model.

validation.check: independent reviewer walks the diagram and confirms each trust-boundary crossing has a threat entry
validation.expect: reviewer initials and date recorded in the document
count equals the number of accepted risks

failure_modes.mode: Diagram is out of date with the code
failure_modes.detection: Reviewer cannot map a code path to a diagram element
failure_modes.response: Return to step 1; model is BLOCKED until the diagram matches the current design
Mark INCONCLUSIVE; assign owners and dates, or record explicit risk acceptance

failure_modes.mode: Risk accepted by the author of the feature
failure_modes.detection: Approver equals implementer in the residual risk log
failure_modes.response: Reject; the security-architect or risk owner must accept

worked_example: ILLUSTRATIVE: A new file-upload endpoint crosses the browser-to-API boundary. Enumerated threats include oversized or malicious files (denial of service, malware storage) and path traversal in filenames. Mitigations: size limit and content-type allow-list at the gateway, random server-side object names, virus scan before the file becomes readable. Each maps to an integration test and to DAST scope in stage 100.
